assumptions: Nominal load ignores bit stuffing; worst-case adds the maximum possible stuff bits.
Bit rate is user-supplied and not verified against the log.
Classical CAN frames only; CAN FD frames are excluded from load figures.
Load is computed per 1-second window from first-frame time.

anomalies.detail: No BMS_Pack for 1.50s (expected every 100 ms, about 14 frames missing)
anomalies.method: Time between consecutive frames of the same message is compared with its expected cycle time (rules file, then DBC GenMsgCycleTime, then the median period observed in the log). A gap larger than gap_factor x expected cycle is reported.
possible_causes: Transmitting ECU reset or power interruption
Bus-off, wiring or arbitration problem
The logger dropped frames (buffer overflow or trigger gap)

anomalies.detail: MC_Checksum is 0x7A but crc8_sae_j1850 over the payload gives 0x0D at 20.001s (3 consecutive frames until 20.041s)
anomalies.method: The configured checksum algorithm is recomputed over the covered payload bytes and compared with the transmitted checksum signal.
possible_causes: Payload corruption
The configured algorithm or covered bytes do not match the ECU's implementation

anomalies.detail: SOC reached 105 (allowed 0 to 100), 3 frame(s) from 20.00s to 20.20s
anomalies.method: Every decoded value of the signal is compared with the configured limits (DBC minimum/maximum, or a user threshold). Consecutive violating frames of the same message are merged into one event.
possible_causes: Sensor or ECU fault
Scaling/offset in the DBC differs from what the transmitter uses
A genuine out-of-limit physical condition

anomalies.method: The configured rolling counter is expected to increase by one (modulo its range) on every frame of its message; any other step is reported.
possible_causes: Frames were lost or duplicated between transmitter and logger

anomalies.detail: ID 0x6A0 is not in the DBC (2 frames)
anomalies.method: The frame's identifier and format (11-bit/29-bit) match no message in the DBC.

Traffic from a node or channel not covered by the DBC
A corrupted identifier

limitations: Findings marked 'confirmed_violation' mean a configured rule (DBC range, user threshold, counter or checksum definition) was broken in the data. 'observed_anomaly' means a deviation from an expectation; it is not proof of a fault.
Possible causes are hypotheses for the engineer to check. This tool does not confirm them.
Expected cycle times come from the rules file, then the DBC GenMsgCycleTime attribute, then the median period seen in the log (an estimate, marked as such).
A DBC signal range of [0|0] is treated as 'no limit defined'.
Bus load is an estimate for classical CAN; CAN FD frames are excluded.
Checksum algorithms and rolling counters are never guessed; only those declared in the rules are checked.
Event-triggered messages without a cycle time have no gap detection beyond the log-median estimate.

Lines the log reader cannot parse are skipped by python-can without notice; for .asc and .log files the tool compares frame-like lines with parsed frames and reports any difference. .csv and .blf files cannot be checked this way.
A payload longer than the DBC message length is decoded with the DBC layout and the extra bytes are ignored.
CAN FD frames are decoded with the DBC message definition; bit-rate switching and the data-phase bit rate are not evaluated.
